frontalLowTailPrompt: Tail stays BELOW the rump: hidden or beside HIND PAWS in front view, never by shoulders/head. Still body/head.
seedMargin: Leave TWO clear pixels on all four canvas edges for animation; keep the silhouette compact and centered.
commonMotion: one clear pixel at ALL 32x32 edges. Small inward motion. Fixed camera, size, position, markings, eyes and crisp palette. No props or text.
rearView: No visible eyes, nose, mouth or chest. Rear head only in ALL frames, including the final hold; no shoulder glance.

tailCarriage.LOW: Tail stays BELOW the rump, never over the back. Front view: hidden behind hind legs, only a low tip may show.
tailCarriage.LEVEL: Tail stays at rump height in every view; wag laterally, never over the back.
tailCarriage.HIGH: Keep the same raised tail height in all views; wag laterally around that height.
tailCarriage.CURLED: Keep the same curled-over-back tail in all views; only a small lateral wag.
tailCarriage.UNKNOWN: Keep approved tail anatomy; never invent a curl or raised tail. Hidden parts may remain hidden.

actions.IDLE: Quiet breath/blink only, at most 1px. Fixed tail and planted paws; NO wag cycle. Hidden tail stays hidden.
actions.WALK: Slow four-legged walk IN PLACE. Small alternating steps, paws lift above the planted baseline, never below.
actions.RUN: Compact four-legged run IN PLACE, short coordinated strides above the planted paw baseline.
actions.SNIFF: Tuck chin inward, lower nose BETWEEN front paws, sniff, lift head. Never extend muzzle forward.
actions.TAIL_WAG: Tail alone wags left-right in DOG BODY coordinates, no vertical pumping. Still body/paws. Side view: subtle foreshortening.
actions.BACK_OFF: Small reverse walking steps IN PLACE, same facing; paws lift upward, centered body.
actions.SIT: Fold hind legs; lower rump between planted paws. End seated, head fixed. Tuck tail beside haunch, complete tip INSIDE frame through final hold; never stretch outward.
actions.LIE_DOWN: Tuck legs inward, lower chest. End lying, hold. Locked head orientation and close tail.

corrections.CANVAS_CLIPPING: Reduce outward reach; tuck tail/muzzle/paws away from ALL edges.
corrections.DIRECTION_DRIFT: Lock head facing through the final frame; rear face stays hidden.
corrections.TAIL_CARRIAGE: Restore shared tail height; never pump it vertically.
corrections.IDENTITY_DRIFT: Restore approved coat, ears, muzzle, eyes and proportions.
corrections.ACTION_MISSING: Show requested motion inside the safe silhouette.
corrections.DETACHED_PIXELS: No detached pixels; keep tail connected.
corrections.IDLE_MOTION: IDLE: fix tail to seed; only tiny breath/blink.

reviewInstructions: DIRECTION_DRIFT: a different facing direction, including a north SIT final frame showing eyes or muzzle. North hides the face through the final hold.

TAIL_CARRIAGE: tail contradicts shared carriage; LOW stays below rump/back. A front low tail may be occluded. For TAIL_WAG only, wag along the dog lateral body axis, not up/down; side-view motion is subtle foreshortening.
IDENTITY_DRIFT: changed coat, ears, face or unexplained body proportions. Expected sitting/lying posture changes are acceptable.

IDLE_MOTION: IDLE is quiet breathing/blinking with planted paws and a stationary tail matching the seed. Reject repeated tail swishing, tail lifting or a new tail appearing above the head. At most one native pixel of breathing is allowed; subtle color changes are acceptable. This restriction does not apply to TAIL_WAG or other actions.
ACTION_MISSING: requested motion absent. IDLE may use subtle breathing only. TAIL_WAG may be occluded or foreshortened; do not require an invented raised tail.
DISCONTINUITY: large pose, position or scale jump between neighbors. SIT ends seated and holds; WALK is an in-place gait.
Canvas clipping is checked separately from original alpha pixels. Never infer cropping from the contact sheet grid.

Use the supplied native-pixel measurements to distinguish motion from minor shading. alphaStable means all nine transparency masks are identical: the silhouette does not grow, shrink or translate. subtleShadingOnly additionally means every visible RGB channel stays within 24/255 of frame 0; this is measured color variation, not evidence of a standing-to-crouching scale jump. Such small shading is acceptable for IDLE. Do not invent large silhouette motion from the layout or lighting of the contact sheet. These measurements do NOT prove identity, eye form, facing or action correctness; still report clear visible internal defects. Never suppress clipping or other independently detected issues.

SIT: inspect the tail through descent AND the final seated hold. Keep the approved anatomy tucked beside the haunch. A missing or bluntly amputated tip is IDENTITY_DRIFT even when the remaining pixels clear the border. Never fix a tail by shrinking the whole dog or replacing seated frames with a standing pose.

EYES: compare open-eye frames with the approved seed: keep pupil shape, position and local contrast. A brief natural blink is allowed. Eyes that stay erased, become hollow rings, or merge into fur in open-eye frames are IDENTITY_DRIFT. North has no face; do not invent eyes.

regressions.expected: Preserve the v11 real 7/12 result, including three new SIT failures and both side IDLE failures. IDLE uses exact frame-zero pairs. Other actions use all four approved direction references and all nine sequential frames, preserving expected sitting/lying transitions and hidden anatomy context. Do not force a pass or remove raw-edit verdicts. Legacy mirrored IDLE may receive one explicit own-seed fallback with its recorded count increasing from 3 to 4; retain every prior grant/hash and replay old requests without spending again. No automatic extra repair budget.

Preserve the actual v10 failures and immutable source images. Show only the matching approved direction and all nine exact frames adjacent to repeated frame 0; every pair uses identical 4x scale and the full canvas including frame 8. Pixel measurements do not force a pass and false subtleShadingOnly does not imply a defect. Live v11 model accuracy remains unverified until deployment.

Keep the actual raw and restored images and Luna failures. Their nine alpha masks are identical, with maximum RGB channel differences of 17 and 15. Send these measurements to vision and retain its verdict; do not force a pass. Older real moving-tail frames must remain detectable, and high-contrast internal changes must never be treated as subtle shading. Live rereview after deployment remains required.
LOW contract must reject a tail above the back
Reject visible eyes/muzzle in final frame 8; do not delete that frame

Reject the whole edited strip before masking or replacing frame 0. Recorded edit has edge contact on all nine frames; frames 1, 5, 8 also contain detached pixels. Reuse only a separately reviewed passing opposite-side tail, preserving the target body.
Server combines raw edit and restored seed/palette verdicts; raw frame 0 failure blocks final approval. Rechecking retains the raw edit hash.

Replay all nine original frames in all four directions. Reject large silhouette excursions even when vision reports no issues; retain original defects. Never slow the entire clip or drop frames to hide wagging. A tail-only fix must not conceal remaining body motion findings.

Original frames 3–8 touch the right edge; reject all six including final hold frame 8, even after a vision pass. Reviewed local tail-only repair clears the border while preserving body pixels and all nine frames. The dog-specific mask is not a generic automatic repair; future generation must tuck the full tail beside the seated haunch.

Block seed approval and all paid motion generation if any visible eye view fails or is uncertain. Recheck every regenerated seed independently; retain originals and receipts. The recorded examples are visual failures, not deterministic coordinate masks.

Actual Luna response reports north readability NOT_VISIBLE and style PASS. Do not invent EYE_DIRECTION from rendering PASS; retain EYE_READABILITY failures in the visible views. Recheck stored images after a rule change without resetting repair counts or submitting another PixelLab request.

Record original four-view failures before repair. AI pass alone is not positive training evidence: require matching human seed approval. Blinded replay must retain known good seeds and reject bad seeds before a lesson reaches another dogs initial generation and seed review. Preserve source photo hashes, budgets, native pixels and motion lesson scopes.

tailEdit.common: Repair ONLY this dog tail-wag animation. Preserve its exact face, ears, coat, body, feet, size and direction. Redraw a COMPLETE short gently curved DOWNWARD tail attached to the rump, with full dark outline and tip visible in EVERY frame. Small sideways wag below the rump, never horizontal or above the back. Tuck the tip toward the hind paws and body. ONE transparent pixel at ALL edges in every frame. Native 32x32, transparent, no resizing, blur, scenery or detached pixels. Fixed body/camera. Smooth cyclic tail motion.
tailEdit.south: Front: tail stays behind the hind legs, only a tiny low tip at ankle height may show. Never attach a tail to neck or chest.
tailEdit.north: Rear: tail stays below the rump and wags sideways close to the hind legs. Face stays hidden.
tailEdit.west: The tail is on the right. Keep its entire curve inside the frame close to the rear leg.
tailEdit.east: The tail is on the left. Keep its entire curve inside the frame close to the rear leg.

idleTailCarriage.LOW: Keep the low seed tail still below rump; hidden in front or beside hind paws.
idleTailCarriage.LEVEL: Keep the level seed tail fixed at rump height.
idleTailCarriage.HIGH: Keep the raised seed tail fixed at its approved height.
idleTailCarriage.CURLED: Keep the seed tail curl and position fixed.
idleTailCarriage.UNKNOWN: Keep seed tail shape and position fixed. If hidden, keep hidden; never add a tail above the head.

seedEyes.prevention: Soft filled dark pupils, distinct from fur, with a tiny muted catchlight. No hollow eye rings, white eyeballs, angry slits or merged black sockets. Match eye size and placement across views; rear has no eyes.
seedEyes.correction: Fix eye readability and rounded filled pupil shape before animation; preserve this dog and the approved art style.
reviewInstructions: Judge new seeds independently against the approved STYLE and photographed IDENTITY. These seeds are unapproved; never treat a flawed seed as a correct reference.

In south, both eyes must read separately from the surrounding coat and muzzle. In west/east the visible eye must read clearly. Compare eye placement, scale and rounded filled pupil treatment across views. North must show no eyes or face.

Accept compact dark filled pupils and a restrained small catchlight. Reject hollow ring or socket eyes, large white eyeballs, angry slash-shaped eyes, misaligned pupils, or eyes that disappear into dark fur. A dark coat still needs readable local contrast without changing coat identity.

Do not demand photorealistic eyes, identical coat colors across dogs, or extra sparkle. Preserve the approved soft pixel-art style. Return UNCERTAIN when eye form cannot be confidently judged; uncertainty does not pass.
Identity compares visible coat/markings, ears, muzzle and puppy/body proportions with the real photo. Do not infer temperament. The style reference supplies rendering only, never the dog identity.

For north with no face or eyes, readability is NOT_VISIBLE. style may be NOT_VISIBLE or PASS for appropriate rendering; a style PASS alone is never evidence of visible eyes. North showing face or eyes must have readability FAIL. A style FAIL or UNCERTAIN still fails quality.

learning.positiveEvidence: AI-passing seeds plus a hash-bound human seed approval
learning.validation: Blinded positive/negative replay with original photo and all four seeds; a rule must preserve immutable gates
learning.note: v7 and v8 eye verdicts used different rules; same-condition nondeterminism has not been established.

reviewPresentation.instruction: A paired review shows only the matching-direction approved seed and nine FRAME 0/current-frame pairs. Each left image repeats frame 0; only the labeled right images form the animation. All images have uniform 4x nearest-neighbor scaling: one native pixel equals four displayed pixels. A false subtleShadingOnly value is NOT a defect verdict; a brief blink can create a high RGB difference without a large pose change. Report concrete visible motion beyond the allowed one native pixel, not merely the presence of changed colors or the displacement between grid cells. Continue checking identity, eyes, direction, action, and actual tail motion independently.
